summary: Educated at Bromsgrove School, King Edward's School, and St John's College, Oxford (~1877–1881), he held a post at University College London (~1892–1911) and taught Mortimer Wheeler.
A linguist, Ernout held positions at the University of Lille (1913–1924), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1919–1951), University of Paris (~1927–1944), and Collège de France (1941–1951).

Working in Sinology and philosophy, Forke studied at the University of Geneva and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1903–1923), Humboldt University (~1904–1923), and University of Hamburg (~1923–1935).

A scholar of Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Foucher studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Sylvain Lévi at the EPHE. He directed the EFEO (1905) and held a professorship at the University of Paris (1929–1936).

Gell studied at Cambridge under Edmund Leach and completed his Ph.D. at the LSE. He lectured at the University of Sussex (~1972–1974), Australian National University (1974), and London School of Economics (1979), becoming a British Academy Fellow.

Specializing in Indology and linguistics, Hillebrandt studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at Breslau and Martin Haug at Munich. He spent his career at the University of Breslau as a Sanskrit professor (1883) and chair holder (1887–1921).

An archaeology and linguistics scholar, Körte studied at the University of Bonn (~1886–1890). He served on the faculties of Bonn, Greifswald, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig University (~1917–1934).

An Indologist and linguist, Ludwig studied at Berlin under Albrecht Weber and at Vienna. After qualifying at Vienna in 1858, he became a professor of comparative linguistics at Charles University (1860, full professor 1871).

Educated at King Edward's School and Cambridge (~1902–1906), he held academic posts at the University of Sydney (~1926–1931), University of Chicago (~1931–1937), University of Oxford (~1937–1946), and FESP in São Paulo (~1942–1944).

A linguist, Harris studied at the University of Massachusetts Amherst and Harvard University (~1973–1976). She held academic posts at Vanderbilt University (~1979–2002) and the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~2009).

A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Turner earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisors Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, also studying with Saw Tun, Daw Than Than Win, John Okell, and Carol S. Anderson.
Specializing in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, Jones studied under doctoral supervisor Martin King Whyte, as well as Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret Dornish.

Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Patel completed her bachelor's degree at Mount Holyoke College and earned a PhD from Harvard University (~1993–2000). She became an associate professor at the University of California, Irvine (~2007).

Specializing in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Grapard earned his Ph.D. from INALCO. He served as ISF Professor of Shinto Studies at the University of California (~1985–2012) and Professor Emeritus at UCSB.

A philosopher, Gibbard earned degrees from Swarthmore College and Harvard University. He held faculty posts at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and served as a professor at the University of Michigan (1977–2016).
Specializing in Sinology, Barr received his doctorate from the University of Oxford in 1983 and served as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College (attested 2001).
An Indologist, Thrasher completed his doctorate under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1969–1977) alongside traditional Indian teachers, and later worked at the Library of Congress (~1986).
Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Dickson earned an MA at McGill University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Lara Braitstein and also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

An Indologist and archaeologist, Führer earned a PhD from Würzburg and studied under Georg Bühler. He held posts at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, the Lucknow State Museum, the Archaeological Survey of India, and later the Christian Catholic Church.
A scholar in linguistics, Müller held library appointments at Palacký University Olomouc (1874–1879), Graz University Library as director (1879), and Vienna University Library (~1867–1901).
